profile.subseg: LT AB Cables; LT XLPE/PVC Cables; Aluminum Conductors (AAC/AAAC/ACSR)
profile.themes: EPC Expansion; Capacity Doubling; Pan-India Vendor Approvals; Data Center & Solar Cables Entry

bull_bear.body: IPO proceeds (Rs. 96 Cr.) used for Dankuni facility acquisition and machinery; future capex funded by internal accruals and potential debt/equity infusion for EPC execution; no dividend policy mentioned
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: EPC competition from KEC, Polycab, Calcutta-based players; execution risk in new Dankuni ramp-up; working capital pressure from EPC projects; raw material price spikes beyond PV clause coverage; delayed government payments (minor, 10-20 days)
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Highly confident, forward-looking, and execution-focused; clear roadmap for capacity doubling, EPC entry, and pan-India expansion; transparent on capex needs and funding strategy; emphasis on operational discipline and market share capture
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: EPC division led by ex-30-year veteran Rajesh Jhunjhunwala signals serious intent; vendor approvals in Punjab/Himachal are not just geographic but strategic to avoid losing bids due to lack of eligibility; Rs. 286 Cr. order book includes legacy orders, but new EPC pipeline is the real growth lever
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

business.body: Cables: 70-80% of revenue; Conductors: growing segment; EPC: new division, targeting 150-200 Cr. revenue in FY27; HTLS, MVCC, AL-59, 11kV HT cables under development
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| EPC expansion exposes JD Cables to capital-intensive, low-margin competition | Laser Cables | loser | Medium | Smaller regional EPC player with limited capacity; JD's vertical integration and IPO-funded scale will erode its tender competitiveness |
| Rising demand for transmission-distribution cables from RDSS and grid projects | Power Grid Corporation of India | beneficiary | High | JD Cables' vendor approvals and capacity expansion directly enable it to capture more RDSS-related cable supply contracts |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

latest_quarter.body: EBITDA margin expanded to 15.85% due to scale and pricing power; raw material (Cu/Al) price volatility mitigated by PV clauses in government tenders; no hedging, but strong supplier relationships and inventory management
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue growth: Target Rs. 350-360 Cr. for FY26, Rs. 500-600 Cr. for FY27, Rs. 1,000 Cr. by FY27-28; Margin: EBITDA to remain 15-16%, PAT margins stable; Order inflow: Targeting Rs. 60 Cr. in pending EPC tenders, more to follow; Capex/Commissioning: Rs. 6-7 Cr. for cable division in H2FY26, total capex ~Rs. 160-170 Cr. to reach Rs. 1,000 Cr. order book
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Rs. 286.21 Cr. as of Sep 30, 2025; 12-18 month execution horizon; Rs. 60 Cr. in pending EPC tenders awaiting results
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Entry into data center copper cables, solar cables, house wire (via distributorship), and OPGW in future; pan-India vendor approvals in Rajasthan, Mizoram, and others pending
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: JD Cables doubled its order book to Rs. 286 Cr. and is aggressively expanding capacity via a new Dankuni facility, with conductor division commissioning in Dec 2025-Jan 2026 to double output by March 2026, while entering EPC to capture forward integration upside and target Rs. 1,000 Cr. order book by FY27-28.
